'''''Dianella sandwicensis''''', the Hawaiian lily, is a species of [[Dianella (plant)|flax lily]] native to [[Hawaii]] and [[New Caledonia]].<ref name="Kew">{{cite POWO |id=533865-1 |title=''Dianella sandwicensis'' |access-date=20 November 2023}}</ref> In Hawaiian it is called {{lang|haw|ʻukiʻuki}}. Neal (1965) reports that historically, Hawaiians used the berries to make blue dye for [[kapa]]. They also used the leaves for thatching house walls.<ref name="Neal">{{cite book |last1=Neal |first1=Marie C. |title=In Gardens of Hawaii |date=1965 |publisher=Bishop Museum Press |location=Honolulu |pages=191–192 |url=https://archive.org/details/ingardensofhawai0000mari/ |access-date=19 November 2023}}</ref>

When sterile, ''Dianella sandwicensis'' is similar in appearance to ''[[Machaerina angustifolia]]''.<ref name="PCSU">{{cite book |last1=Medeiros |first1=A.C. |last2=Loope |first2=L.L. |last3=Chimera |first3=C.G. |title=Flowering plants and gymnosperms of Haleakala National Park. Honolulu (HI) |date=1998 |publisher=University of Hawaii at Manoa |pages=35 |url=http://hdl.handle.net/10125/7333 |access-date=19 November 2023}}</ref>

Its leaves are simple, linear-lanceolate shaped, and usually have entire margins.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Wagner |first=Warren |title=Manual of the flowering plants of Hawai'i. |last2=Herbst |first2=Derral |last3=Sohmer |first3=S.H. |date=1990 |publisher=University of Hawaii Pres}}</ref> Also typically blue to purple in color with its anther being orange.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Degner |first=Otto |title=Flora Hawaiiensis: the new illustrated flora of the Hawaiian Islands |date=1932 |publisher=Cornell University}}</ref> Wolkis et al., describes the flowers as "sweet-scented".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wolkis |first=D |last2=Baskin |first2=C |last3=Baskin |first3=J |last4=Osunkoya |first4=O |date=2018 |title=Dormancy-breaking and germination requirements of seeds of the Hawaiian endemic Dianella sandwicensis (Xanthorrhoeaceae) |journal=Australian Journal of Botany |volume=66 |issue=3 |pages=213-217}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Commonly found in the ridges on Oahu, Maui, and Kauai.<ref name=":0" /> It has not been confirmed, but it is entirely possible that this specific trope of Dianella is also found in the Marquesas, according to Brown's specimen collection.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brown |first=F.B.H. |date=1930 |title=New Polynesian plants: B. P. Bishop Mus. |journal=Occ, Papers |volume=9 |issue=4}}</ref>

==Human use and cultural significance==
''D. sandwicensis'' has been historically used as a blue dye for clothing.<ref>{{Cite book |last=St John |first=H |title=Review of Mrs. Sinclair's "Indigenous Flowers of the Hawaiian Islands" Hawaiian Plant Studies |date=1954 |publisher=University of Hawai'i Press}}</ref>
